Rashi on Makkot 15a:11:1.hebrew: וגמר מיניה - דכי היכי דמוציא שם רע לא לקי בגירושין אם החזיר, אונס נמי לא לקי:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:11:1.english: And [the rapist] is derived from him - Just as a defamer is not flogged for [his] divorcing [his wife] if he takes [her] back, so too a rapist is not flogged.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:11:2.hebrew: אי בק"ו - מה מוציא שם רע, שלוקה ומשלם בתחלתו, אינו לוקה בגירושין — אונס, לא כל שכן:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:11:2.english: If by an a fortiori inference - [If] a defamer, who is flogged and pays at the outset, is not flogged for the divorce — a rapist, all the more so [he should not be flogged]:

Rashi on Makkot 15a:12:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - הא דתניא באונס מחזיר ואינו לוקה, טעמא משום דעל כרחך לאו שניתק לעשה הוא. דאמר קרא "כל ימיו" — לא הוה ליה למיכתב, אלא "לא יוכל לשלחה". מאי "כל ימיו"? הכי קאמר: לא תהא בשילוחיה כל ימיו, אלא יחזירנה. ועל כרחך "עמוד והחזר" קאמר. והכי קאמר: "ולו תהיה לאשה" — אם שלחה, שלא יהו שילוחיה לכל ימיו, הרי העשה אחר העברת הלאו:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:12:1.english: Rather, Rava said - This [law] that was taught — that a rapist remarries [her] and does not receive lashes — the reason is that you must say it is a prohibition that is rectified by a positive commandment. For the verse says "all his days" — [the verse] did not need to write it; it should have written only "he may not send her away." What is "all his days"? This is what it is saying: He shall not be in the state of sending her away all his days, but rather he must take her back. And you must say it means "arise and remarry." And this is what it is saying: "And she shall be his wife" — if he sent her away, so that his sending away not remain for all his days, behold, the positive commandment comes after the violation of the prohibition.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:13:1.hebrew: והא לא דמי לאויה - הא דאמר ר' יוחנן לא תעשה שקדמו עשה לוקין עליו, הא לא דמי לאויה ללאו דחסימה, שאין בו עשה, והוא סמוך לפרשת מלקות:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:13:1.english: But isn't its prohibition dissimilar - Regarding that which Rabbi Yoḥanan said, that one is flogged for a prohibition preceded by a positive commandment: its prohibition is not similar to the prohibition of muzzling, which has no positive commandment [attached to it], and which is adjacent to the passage [that speaks] of lashes.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:13:2.hebrew: מיגרע גרע - וכי משום שכתב בו הכתוב עשה יתירא, האם הלאו מתמעט בתמיהה:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:13:2.english: Does it lessen? - Is it so that, because the verse wrote a positive commandment in its regard, the prohibition is diminished? This is stated as a question of astonishment.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:14:1.english: That [verse] came only to sever the prohibition - A positive commandment that can be fulfilled only after the prohibition has been transgressed comes to sever the prohibition from the punishment of lashes.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:15:1.hebrew: הניחא למאן דתני בטלו ולא בטלו אלא למאן דתני קיימו ולא קיימו מאי איכא למימר - הא דאמרת כל ימיו בעמוד והחזר קאי, עשיתו לאו שניתק לעשה, והרחבת לו זמן לקיום העשה כל ימיו. ולדבריך הא דתניא מחזיר ואינו לוקה, לעולם קאמר, כל זמן שיכול לומר אני מחזיר, אין ב"ד מלקין אותו. הניחא למאן דתני לקמן בלאו הניתק לעשה: בטל את העשה — חייב על הלאו, לא בטל את העשה — פטור, שהלאו תלוי בביטול העשה, ואינו נגמר עד שיבטל את העשה בידים ביטול עולם שלא יוכל להתקיים עוד, איכא למימר כל ימיו יש לו תקנה בחזרה, שאין מבטל את העשה אלא א"כ מדירה שלא תהנה ממנו, נדר שאין לו הפרה כדלקמן. אלא למאן דתני: קיים את העשה — פטור, לא קיימו — חייב, שהעשה תיקונו של לאו הוא, ואין הלאו תלוי בביטול העשה, שמשעה שעבר הלאו נגמר, אבל העשה ניתן לעקור המלקות, ולכשיבא לבית דין או יקיים העשה ויפטר או ילקה, ליכא למימר כל ימיו בעמוד והחזר קאי כדקאמרת, שאם לא יחזירנה מיד כשיבא לב"ד ילקוהו, דהא ליכא למימר יקיים לאחר זמן, דא"כ לא קיים, היכי דמי? לעולם הוא יכול לומר אני מקיים:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:15:1.english: This works out well according to the one who teaches "he nullified it" or "he did not nullify it"; but according to the one who teaches "he fulfilled it" or "he did not fulfill it," what is there to say? - This statement of yours, that all his days he is standing [under the obligation] to arise and remarry, [means] you have made it a prohibition that is linked to a positive commandment, and you have extended for him the time for fulfilling the positive commandment [to] all his days. And according to your words, the statement in the baraita "he remarries her and is not flogged" is said to apply always: as long as he can say "I will remarry her," the court does not flog him. This works out well according to the one who teaches below, regarding a prohibition linked to a positive commandment: if he nullified the positive commandment, he is liable for the prohibition; if he did not nullify the positive commandment, he is exempt. For the prohibition depends on the nullification of the positive commandment, and it is not completed until he actively nullifies the positive commandment with a permanent nullification, so that it can no longer be fulfilled. [Then] it is possible to say that all his days he has a remedy through remarrying her, since he does not nullify the positive commandment unless he binds her by a vow not to derive benefit from him, a vow that has no annulment, as [stated] below. But according to the one who teaches: if he fulfilled the positive commandment he is exempt, [and] if he did not fulfill it he is liable — since the positive commandment is the rectification of the prohibition, and the prohibition does not depend on the nullification of the positive commandment, for from the moment he transgressed, the prohibition is complete, but the positive commandment is given [as a means] to uproot the lashes, so that when he comes to court he will either fulfill the positive commandment and be exempt, or be flogged — it cannot be said that all his days he is standing [under the obligation] to arise and remarry, as you said; for if he does not remarry her immediately when he comes to court, they will flog him. For it cannot be said that he may fulfill it at a later time, since if so, he has not fulfilled it. How [then] is this the case? [For] he can always say, "I will fulfill it."

Rashi on Makkot 15a:1:1.hebrew: אמרו לו - אחרים ששמעוהו משמו ולא שמעוהו מפיו, אמרו לרבי יוחנן: אמרת דבר זה?:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:1:1.english: They said to him - Others, who had heard it in his name but had not heard it from his own mouth, [said to Rabbi Yoḥanan]: Did you say this statement?

Rashi on Makkot 15a:1:2.hebrew: אמר להם לא - רבי יוחנן חזר בו:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:1:2.english: He said to them: No - [Rabbi Yoḥanan] retracted his statement.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:1:3.hebrew: כתיבא ותנינא - מצינו כתוב לא תעשה שקדמו עשה, ותנינן עליה דלוקין, ולא סגי ליה בקיום העשה:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:1:3.english: It is written and we learned - We find a prohibition written that is preceded by a positive commandment, and we learned about it that [the violators] are flogged, and the fulfillment of the positive commandment does not suffice for him.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:1:4.hebrew: תנינא הבא אל המקדש טמא - קא חשיב ליה באלו הן הלוקין:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:1:4.english: We learned: One who enters the Temple impure - [The Mishnah] counts him among "These are the ones who receive lashes."

Rashi on Makkot 15a:2:1.hebrew: משום דקשיא ליה אונס - נערה בתולה, דאשכחן ביה לא תעשה שקדמו עשה, דכתיב (דברים כ״ב:כ״ט) ולו תהיה לאשה, לא יוכל לשלחה. ותניא עלה: שיקיים את העשה — אם גירשה, ויחזירנה, ויפטור. אלמא, לאו שניתק לעשה חשיב ליה:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:2:1.english: Because the case of the rapist is difficult for him - [This refers to] a virgin young woman, regarding whom we find a prohibition that is preceded by a positive commandment, as it is written (Deuteronomy 22:29): "And she shall be his wife; he may not send her away." And it is taught about this [verse] in a baraita: [The rapist] fulfills the positive commandment — if he divorced her, he must take her back, and he is exempt [from lashes]. Evidently, [Rabbi Yehuda] considers it a prohibition that is turned into a positive commandment.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:2:2.hebrew: אם ישראל הוא - שיכול לקיים את העשה ויחזירנה, מחזיר ואינו לוקה:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:2:2.english: If he is an Israelite - For he is able to fulfill the positive commandment and take her back, he takes her back and is not flogged.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:2:3.hebrew: ואם כהן הוא - שאסור בגרושה, לוקה ואינו מחזיר:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:2:3.english: And if he is a priest - who is forbidden to marry a divorcée, he is flogged and does not remarry [her].

Rashi on Makkot 15a:3:1.hebrew: ואמאי - אם ישראל הוא מחזיר ואינו לוקה, קשה אם איתא לדרבי יוחנן, הא לא תעשה שקדמו עשה הוא:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:3:1.english: And why? - If he is a non-priest, he remarries her and is not flogged — [this is difficult], if Rabbi Yochanan's [view] is correct, since this is a prohibition that was preceded by a positive commandment!

Rashi on Makkot 15a:4:1.hebrew: אמר עולא - האי לאו שניתק לעשה הוא. דאי לאו לנתוקי לאוי אתא האי עשה, לא הוה מצטריך למכתביה. דאי לתחלתו, ולומר שישאנה, לא יאמר "לו תהיה לאשה", ונגמר ממוציא שם רע, דכתיב ביה נמי "ולו תהיה לאשה, לא יוכל לשלחה":
Rashi on Makkot 15a:4:1.english: Ulla said - This is a prohibition that is converted into a positive commandment. For if this positive commandment did not come to resolve the prohibition, it would not have needed to be written. For if it were meant for the outset, to say that he should marry her, [the verse] need not say "and she shall be his wife," and we would derive it from the one who defames, about whom it is also written "and she shall be his wife; he may not send her away" (Deuteronomy 22:19).

Rashi on Makkot 15a:5:1.hebrew: אם אינו ענין - לפני הגירושין, ולומר שישאנה, תנהו ענין לאחר הגירושין, לומר שאם שלחה יחזירנה, ותהיה לו לאשה, ויפטר מן הלאו:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:5:1.english: If it is not relevant - before the divorce, and to say that he should marry her, apply it to the matter after the divorce, to say that if he sent her away he shall take her back, and she shall be a wife to him, and he is exempted from the prohibition.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:6:1.hebrew: ואכתי - הא איצטריך למיכתביה "וישנו ענין לפניו", דאי לא כתביה, אונס ממוציא שם רע לא גמר. דאנא אמינא: מה למוציא שם רע — דין הוא שיקנסוהו לכנסה — שכן לוקה ומשלם בתחלתו, כדכתיב "ויסרו אותו וענשו אותו", ואמרינן בכתובות (דף מו.) "ויסרו" זה מלקות:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:6:1.english: But still - It was needed for [the verse] to write "and the matter [of the rapist] is before him" (a textual hint to compare the two cases), for if it had not written it, one could not derive [the law of] a rapist from a defamer. For I would say: What is notable about a defamer — that it is right to penalize him to marry her — is that he is flogged and pays at the outset, as it is written, "and they shall chastise him and they shall fine him," and we said in Ketubot (46a) that "and they shall chastise him" refers to flogging.

Rashi on Makkot 15a:7:1.hebrew: מה אונס שאינו לוקה - בתחלתו אמר רחמנא "לו תהיה לאשה", מוציא שם רע לא כל שכן:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:7:1.english: If a rapist, who is not flogged - at the outset, the Merciful One said, "And she shall be his wife." Is this not all the more so for the defamer?

Rashi on Makkot 15a:9:1.hebrew: שהרי אשתו היא - שכבר קידשה ונשאה:
Rashi on Makkot 15a:9:1.english: For she is already his wife - For he has already betrothed her and married her.

Tosafot on Makkot 15a:12:1.hebrew: כל ימיו בעמוד - והחזר קאי. פירש בקונטרס דקאי אלא יוכל לשלחה כל ימיו, שילוח שלא יהא כל ימיו. ובפ' עשרה יוחסין (קדושין דף עח.) פירש דקאי אלו תהיה לאשה דלעיל, דהכי קאמר: תהיה לאשה כל ימיו, כלומר, שכל ימיו הוא בלו תהיה לאשה, בעמוד והחזר:
Tosafot on Makkot 15a:12:1.english: "All his days" [is connected to] "arise" - and "and remarry" refers [to the same thing]. Rashi explained that it refers to "[lo yuchal] — he may not send her away all his days" — [that is,] a sending away that shall not be [in force] all his days. But in the chapter Asara Yuchasin (Kiddushin 78a) he explained that it refers to the earlier "she shall be his wife" (lo tihyeh le'ishah), for this is what [the verse] says: "She shall be a wife all his days" — meaning that "all his days" belongs with "she shall be a wife," [and is connected to] "arise and remarry."

Tosafot on Makkot 15a:15:1.hebrew: הניחא למאן דתני בטלו ולא בטלו - פירש בקונטרס: דקאי לשינויא דרבא, דכל ימיו בעמוד והחזר, ויש לו תקנה בהחזרה, שאין מבטל העשה אלא אם כן הדירה, דאז אינו יכול לומר "עדיין אשאנה". אלא למאן דתני "קיימו", מאי איכא למימר? בכולי שמעתתא פירש הקונט' דקיימו, היינו כשמזהירין אותו ב"ד לקיים העשה, הוא מקיימו. וקשה, דאם כן מאי פריך? דלמאן דאמר "קיימו ולא קיימו" אינו "כל ימיו בעמוד והחזר"? הא שפיר משכחת לה דהוי בעמוד והחזר, כל כמה דלא בא לב"ד! לכך נראה דלא מיקרי "קיימו" אלא דוקא כשמקיים העשה אחר שעבר הלאו בתוך כדי דיבור, וכן פי' הקונטרס בפרק שילוח הקן (חולין דף קמא.). ומיהו קצת קשה, דא"כ צריך לפרש הא דקתני "מחזיר ואינו לוקה" שמחזיר מיד בתוך כדי דיבור אחר הגירושין, וכן "המשלח ואינו לוקה", ולא משתמע הכי כלל; דהא משמע דמהדר אתקנתא, היאך יפטר ממלקות, שיחזיר או ישלח, ואפי' אחר כדי דיבור נמי. משמע שבא לשאול עליו לבית דין אם יש לו תקנה; דאי דוקא בתוך כדי דיבור, הכי הוה ליה למימר "אם החזיר אינו לוקה". ושמא יש לישב פירוש הקונטרס דשמעתין, דהכא ליכא למימר דשפיר הוי "כל ימיו בעמוד והחזר", דמשמע לעולם, אף כשבא לב"ד, כל זמן שבידו להחזיר, אפילו מיאן להחזיר כשבא לב"ד. דהא דרשינן ליה מיתורא דכל ימיו, דהכי קאמר: לא יוכל לשלחה שילוחין שיהו שילוחיה כל ימיו, דהיינו באינו מחזיר כלל:
Tosafot on Makkot 15a:15:1.english: "This works out well according to the one who taught: 'he nullified it' or 'he did not nullify it'" - Rashi explained that this refers to Rava's answer, that "all his days he must arise and remarry her," and he has a remedy through remarriage, for he nullifies the positive commandment only if he made her forbidden to him by a vow, for then he cannot say, "I will yet marry her." But according to the one who taught "he fulfilled it," what can be said? Throughout the Talmud, Rashi explained that "he fulfilled it" means that when the court warns him to fulfill the positive commandment, he fulfills it. But this is difficult: if so, what is the Gemara's challenge, that according to the one who says "he fulfilled it or he did not fulfill it," it is not the case that "all his days he must arise and remarry"? Surely it is properly found that he is in the status of "arise and remarry" for as long as he has not come before the court! Therefore it appears that "he fulfilled it" is said only when he fulfills the positive commandment after he transgressed the prohibition, within the time of a short utterance (toch kedei dibbur); and so Rashi explained in the chapter Shilu'ach HaKen (Chullin 141a). However, this is somewhat difficult, for if so, we must explain what the Mishnah teaches, "he remarries her and is not flogged," as meaning that he remarries immediately, within a short utterance after the divorce; and likewise "he sends away and is not flogged." Yet this is not implied at all; for it implies that he is seeking a remedy — how can he be exempted from lashes — that he remarry or send away, even after a short utterance. It implies that he comes to ask the court whether he has a remedy; for if it were specifically within a short utterance, it should have said, "If he remarried, he is not flogged." Perhaps one can resolve Rashi's explanation of our passage: here one cannot say that it is properly "all his days he must arise and remarry," which implies forever, even when he comes before the court, as long as it is in his power to remarry, even if he refused to remarry when he came before the court. For we derive this from the extra word "all his days," which means: he may not send her away with a sending-away such that his sending-away lasts all his days, that is, where he does not remarry her at all:

Tosafot on Makkot 15a:1:1.hebrew: תנינא הבא למקדש טמא - לוקה, משום דלא הוי לאו הניתק לעשה, לפי שקדמו עשה ללאו. וא"ת: דלמא שאני התם, דאיכא תרי לאוי: "ולא יטמאו מחניהם", "ולא יטמאו מקדשי", ולא אתי חד עשה ועקר תרי לאוין, דהכי משנינן בתמורה (דף ד: ושם) גבי "המר ימיר", דמשום הכי לא הוי לאו הניתק לעשה, משום דאיכא תרי לאוין, ולא עקר חד עשה תרי לאוין. וי"ל: דלא דמי, דשאני התם דתרי לאוין סמוכין להדדי — "לא יחליפנו ולא ימיר אותו"; אבל הכא דאינן סמוכים, אי איתא דלא קדמו עשה, הוה ניתק:
Tosafot on Makkot 15a:1:1.english: "We learned: One who enters the Temple impure" - He is flogged, because it is not a prohibition that is resolved by a positive commandment, since the positive commandment preceded the prohibition. And if you say: Perhaps that case is different, because there are two prohibitions there — "and they shall not render their camp impure," and "and they shall not render My sanctuary impure" — and one positive commandment does not come and uproot two prohibitions, as we answer in Temurah (4b, there) regarding "he shall surely substitute": that the reason it is not a prohibition resolved by a positive commandment is that there are two prohibitions, and one positive commandment does not uproot two prohibitions. And one can say: It is not comparable, for there it is different, since the two prohibitions are adjacent to one another — "He shall not exchange it, and he shall not substitute it." But here, where they are not adjacent, if it were so that the positive commandment did not precede, it would be resolved [by it]:

Tosafot on Makkot 15a:2:1.hebrew: אם כהן הוא לוקה ואינו מחזיר - וליכא למימר דאתי עשה ודחי לא תעשה, ועשה שאינו שוה בכל — דהא אי אמרה "לא בעינא ליה", ליכא עשה כלל:
Tosafot on Makkot 15a:2:1.english: If he is a priest, he is flogged and does not remarry her - And one cannot say that the positive commandment [to remarry her] comes and overrides the prohibition, [since this is] a positive commandment that does not apply equally to all [cases] — for if she says, "I do not want him," there is no positive commandment at all:
